To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new approach to single channel source separation using DNNs.

we propose a novel approach for SCSS using DNN that works for source signals with arbitrary energy scale differences and that the DNN initialized by a nonnegative matrix factorization improves the performance of SCSS compared with using nonnegative matrix factorizations alone.
we introduce a novel approach for source separation using deep neural networks that is based on energy minimization and that we show the proposed approach outperforms NMF for source estimation.

the development of a new approach for single channel audio source separation based on DNN architecture.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a DNN to aid in source separation improves the separation performance of NMF.
using a deep neural net for SCSS is an improvement over using NMF for the same problem.
the use of a DNN to classify source spectra improves separation results compared with using NNF for separation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an approach for source separation that uses a DNN to check for the validity of the estimated source signals.
the DNN is able to capture the characteristics of the source signals during the training stage and use it during the separation stage.
the DNN initialized by the NMF estimate can be used to improve the source separation performance in a single channel source separation scenario.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNN is a useful tool for source separation, even in the case when the DNN is not trained with the source signals used in the separation process.
the DNN can be trained to learn the statistical characteristics of the source signals and the DNN model can be used as a prior to improve source separation.
using DNN as a classifier for the separation process improves the quality of separated sources.
